key: cited_stmt_gen___gpt-5__What is the most cost-effective method for improving soil fertility in Mediterranean arable fields: adding compost or growing cover crops?

parts.text:
Given a summary of information and a list of statements extracted from this summary, you must extract the document IDs cited in the summary for each statement. There may be zero or more cited IDs per statement.
Output the statements with their extracted citations as a list of JSON objects.

Summary: In Mediterranean-type climates and countries including Italy and Spain, winter cover crops increased soil organic matter in some or all comparisons across a meta-analysis and multiple replicated, controlled studies, and increased soil nitrogen in some comparisons, though other studies found less or inconsistent nitrogen changes; phosphorus was similar in one study, potassium increased in one study; cover crops also increased microbial biomass and water-stable aggregates in some comparisons [1345]. Across studies from Italy, Spain, Syria, and Turkey, adding compost increased soil organic matter in some or all comparisons and increased soil nutrients in some or all comparisons, with inconsistent nitrogen results and no difference in phosphorus in one study; pH was similar in some studies; compost increased microbial biomass in some or all comparisons and improved soil stability and reduced erosion in some studies [1362].
Statements: ['In Mediterranean-type climates, winter cover crops increased soil organic matter in some or all comparisons.', 'Winter cover crops increased soil nitrogen in some comparisons in Mediterranean-type climates.', 'Some studies found that winter cover crops produced less or inconsistent changes in soil nitrogen.', 'One study showed similar phosphorus levels after using winter cover crops, while another showed an increase in potassium.', 'Cover crops increased microbial biomass in some comparisons.', 'Cover crops increased water-stable aggregates in some comparisons.', 'Across studies from Italy, Spain, Syria, and Turkey, adding compost increased soil organic matter in some or all comparisons.', 'Adding compost increased soil nutrients in some or all comparisons.', 'Studies on adding compost reported inconsistent results for soil nitrogen.', 'One study on adding compost found no difference in soil phosphorus.', 'Soil pH was similar in some studies after adding compost.', 'Compost increased microbial biomass in some or all comparisons.', 'In some studies, adding compost improved soil stability.', 'In some studies, adding compost reduced erosion.']

citations.description: List of citations (action numbers) given for the statement. Can be empty if no citations are given in the summary for this statement.

items.description: An action number (e.g. 250) that supports the statement.
